indicators.label: Blood pressure, upper
indicators.howToMeasure: Use the blood pressure cuff as you were trained. Enter the upper number it shows.
indicators.whyInSpace: In one study of eight astronauts on long flights, average 24-hour blood pressure was about 8 to 10 mmHg lower than before flight; the authors linked this to fluid shifting toward the head and blood vessels relaxing.

indicators.label: Blood pressure, lower
indicators.howToMeasure: Use the blood pressure cuff as you were trained. Enter the lower number it shows.
indicators.whyInSpace: In one study of eight astronauts on long flights, average 24-hour blood pressure was about 8 to 10 mmHg lower than before flight; the authors linked this to fluid shifting toward the head and blood vessels relaxing.

indicators.label: Resting heart rate
indicators.howToMeasure: Measure while resting, as you were trained. Enter the beats per minute (bpm) shown.
indicators.whyInSpace: In one study of eight astronauts on long flights, average 24-hour heart rate stayed about the same as before flight, so a lasting change from your own normal is worth checking.

indicators.label: Body temperature
indicators.howToMeasure: Use the thermometer as you were trained. Enter the reading in degrees Celsius.
indicators.whyInSpace: In one study, resting core temperature rose about 1 °C over roughly 2.5 months in orbit, so the app compares readings with your own in-flight normal as well as with a fixed upper limit.

indicators.label: Fasting blood sugar
indicators.howToMeasure: Measure before eating, using the glucose meter as you were trained. Enter the reading in mg/dL.
indicators.whyInSpace: Some studies report signs of insulin resistance in flight, but the data conflict.

indicators.label: Sleep last night
indicators.howToMeasure: Enter how long you slept last night, in hours. Quarter hours are fine, for example 6.75.
indicators.whyInSpace: Crews are scheduled 8.5 hours of sleep but average about 6.

indicators.label: Mood
indicators.howToMeasure: Tap the number that best matches your mood today: 1 is very low and 5 is very good.
indicators.whyInSpace: Isolation and confinement raise behavioral health risk on long missions.

indicators.label: Reaction time
indicators.howToMeasure: Use the in-app reaction test: tap the target as fast as you can when it appears, five times. The app records your middle result in milliseconds (ms).
indicators.whyInSpace: Long-term sleep loss lowers performance. Our test is a simplified check, not a validated instrument.

indicators.label: Exercise done today
indicators.howToMeasure: Enter the total minutes of exercise you did today.
indicators.whyInSpace: Bone density falls roughly 1 to 1.5% a month without countermeasures; crews are scheduled 2.5 hours of exercise six days a week.

indicators.label: Near-vision check
indicators.howToMeasure: Hold the screen at arm's length and tap the smallest line you can read. This is a self-check, not an eye exam.
indicators.whyInSpace: About two-thirds of long-duration crew show early signs of spaceflight associated neuro-ocular syndrome (SANS), a set of eye and vision changes.
